posts.name: Chaosmancer
posts.cooked:
I think the only part of this contest I don't agree with was Bugbear. I had Bugbear doing to Proletariat what Spite ended up doing, devouring the clones with his stone and becoming more powerful. And it seems his loss was mostly because he was too shocked to be back in existence again that he didn't start fighting until after Proletariat had started beating him with hammers.

 

And still, unless I really misunderstand how that stone works, I would have thought he could recover from that and start ripping the life force from Proletariat ,ike he did Calypso. But, they almost seems like a rigged match where Jansa really should have let Bugbear out sooner so he could be ready to actually fight instead of just popping him back into a place with air and time and expecting him to start fighting immediately.

 

 

Other than that, most of this was really good. I get why some of the fights I got wrong were wrong, and I loved a lot of the later fights that ended up happening. Also, I'm blown away that this is the first time that Baron Blade's Fission Blaster is revealed, and I'm super excited that it could potentially be a card in Luminary's deck. I love that thing in Tactics

I got a mere 29 and no perfect tiers, though a couple that I missed by only one (Bugbear and Ermine), and one by two (Ra and Tempest).  I too thought Bugbear would feed off the Proletariat clones--I fact, I had Proletariat winning at first, then figured Spite would feed off the clones, then realized Bugbear would have done the exact same thing.  I'm kicking myself for not realizing how Lifeline vs. Blood Countess would go--in retrospect that was obvious from the Blood Magic episode--but I horribly botched that bracket anyway, getting literally every other match-up wrong.  I had no idea Biomancer would turn out to be such a respectable combatant in person.

I'm standing by my brackets for "best story," though.  I made a choice to go with good stories over literal "who would win" results, and it went poorly for me.  I think if I'd understood the format better--I thought it would be lots of individual comics, so each one would have to draw an audience on its own merits--I would have done better.

posts.name: rjc917
posts.cooked:
That didn't exactly go as I expected, but I still did decently well.  I was impressed how they pretty much just took the "who would win this fight?" approach rather than trying to set up interesting stories, but it still ended up with interesting stories anyway, even if not some of the ones I had in mind.

Champion: 5 (only mistakes were setting up Ra vs Fanatic and thinking Fanatic could be stopped by lightning)

Tech: 4 (Anything AZ won I had wrong.  That was one of the biggest surprises to me.)

Mystic: 6 (Had everything except Idealist, because I thought Harpy vs Nightmist sounded better.)

Martial: 2 (This was my worst tier.  I was really surprised when they said this was one of the ones that the most people had perfect.  I could have done 3 better if I took Fixer through instead of Wraith like I was thinking I probably should have done, but I really didn't expect Chrono-Ranger or Stuntman to win, despite the fact that I like both of them more than their opponents.)

Conqueror: 5 (Only got Zhu Long wrong.  In hindsight, I never should have expected them to pass up showing people fighting a dragon.)

Cunning: 5 (Had Green Grosser and The Chairman wrong.  I liked the explanation of how Green Grosser beat Ermine, but I felt like "The Chairman makes his own luck" was kind of cheap.  Sure he's a better fighter than Kismet, but he should go to punch her and his wrist breaks or something.)

Eldritch: 5 (Lifeline was my champion, so that didn't work out, but I had everything else right)

Bruiser: 3 (This is the other tier I was second-guessing the most and it turned out I would have done much better if I changed my answers.  Enough other people have complained about Bugbear, so I won't, but yeah.)

Finals: 1 (While I got over half of the preliminary rounds right, only 3 of my tier champions were right, and out of them, Baron Blade was the only one I correctly had winning a fight.  I had Nightmist lose to Lifeline and had Citizen Dawn win and then beat Baron Blade.)

Final score:  36/63, but I could have gotten as high as 43 if I made the changes I was considering.

The Cosmic Contest is the best sort of 'who would win in a fight' discussion. It gives a lot of interesting 'what if?' confrontations, but doesn't give us an ultimate answer of who's the 'best' character, because each fight was so situational. We can all hang onto our favourites, and agree that the Nightmist writers need someone to take them off to one side and have a quiet word about making everyone else look bad. :P

I have a somewhat deserved reputation for being excessively negative, but I have tried hard to combat that tendency since back in my Justifier days. But it’s been a while since I indulged much at all, so I think I have earned the right to at least say that this is one of my least favorite episodes of the early podcast (probably least up to this part apart from small interludes that don’t really count), and that I largely don’t care for the Contest itself as a story in its current form.

BUT! As I often said back when Justifying, perceiving something as “wrong” often makes me become very invested in trying to make it right. And as I listened to this episode, I found an unprecedented degree of desire to rewrite to my satisfaction. Not because I don’t like the concept, although that’s somewhat true, and not because I disagree with many of the match outcomes, although that’s definitely true. But because, in my opinion, a lot of the presented details of how the scenario is presented, both in terms of the participants and of the readers, don’t quite line up as presented. Why Jansa is doing this, why the heroes agree to fight each other with at least close to lethal force, why the villains voluntarily participate against someone definitely using lethal force, what happens as a result of the outcomes, and how the whole thing makes a comic book that would be any good… I’m trying to make all these details add up, and the answers I come up with seem interesting IMO. Interesting enough that there could be a good fanfic in it, though it would be a lot more work than any project I’ve ever come close to completing.

For now, all I’m going to say about my headcanon vision is this. This is the Sentinels OblivAeon version of a certain iconic scene in… (decides the Schmony Schmobbins bit isn’t going to cut it here) …in Retributors: Unbounded Conflict. In that scene, the Nightmist or Argent ripoff character holds up a single finger, and then shortly thereafter names the sequel film. That’s what Jansa has to be doing with this conflict. Tarogath is back from being Deadline, so Jansa again has the Pandemonium Key, and I say that every aspect of how the contest is structured, every finest detail of the rules, was decided based on seeing how every other possible outcome would result either in OblivAeon succeeding and everything being destroyed, or something even worse (eg Bugbear eats everyone up to and including OblivAeon, or Paul VIII makes some error in judgement that turns him into Sciorn Legacy and he saves America by feeding Rainek all the other countries, something outrageous like that which would mandate one of the unfair matchups or improbable upsets or the like). The Key and similar equipment has proven to her satisfaction that everything has to happen within these exactly parameters. That doesn’t mean she calculated everything, at least one of the match outcomes had to have been an upset even by her standard; the heroes and villains get credit for what they did, and the lasting repercussions (eg the end of Dark Visionary) remain. But this wasn’t just Jansa picking an Endling from Earth or anything, this was her ensuring reality would be preserved, however terrible the price.
